title: The Panic That Wasn't
music: Guy Ritchie style British crime-caper groove: punchy breakbeat drums, slap bass, brass stabs, cheeky and fast, about 100 bpm, confident swagger, no vocals.
ambience: Faint vintage radio static, no music.
disclosure: AI-generated images and voice. Facts: Pooley & Socolow (Slate, 2013); Hooper survey via Broadcasting (1938); Radiolab (2010) on Quito, 1949.

shots.say: October thirtieth, nineteen thirty-eight. Orson Welles reads a Martian invasion on CBS radio. Next morning, the papers scream: mass panic. Lovely story. One problem. That night, a ratings firm rang five thousand homes. Two percent said Welles. Not one said news. The big crowd was on NBC, laughing at a ventriloquist's dummy. So who cooked up the panic? Newspapers, sore at radio for nicking their advertisers. The real panic came eleven years later, in Quito, Ecuador. A station burned. People died. Nobody remembers that one. The full film is on AI Broadsheet.
